captions.caption: The lenticular galaxy NGC 2787. This galaxy is a disk galaxy but lacks the large, dominant spiral arm structure seen in the disks of spiral galaxies. Its core is very bright compared to the core of a spiral galaxy. Thin rings of dust can be seen in the galaxy's disk.
captions.alt_text: The bright core of this galaxy is surrounded by a much fainter disk. This faint disk has thin dark rings.
captions.credit: NASA/ESA and The Hubble Heritage Team
